summary: A dense worker-placement engine-builder set in 16th-century Prague, where players train rabbi-students and grow golems that wander a shared neighborhood board, delivering benefits until they grow dangerously powerful. It's from the same team behind Grand Austria Hotel and Lorenzo il Magnifico, and plays with a similar flavor of tightly interlocking action-selection systems.
praised: deep, rewarding engine-building with many viable paths
clever risk/reward tension in growing versus destroying golems
high production values and strong table presence
good replayability from variable player powers and setup
criticised: can suffer from analysis paralysis with so many options
some find it a busy "salad" of subsystems rather than a focused design

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking with golems on a shared board
interaction.detail: Players take turns on shared action spaces, so popular spots get blocked, and golems move through a shared neighborhood map where they can affect or threaten other players' students and buildings. Each player otherwise develops their own tableau of cards and resources largely independently.

scoring.how_you_win: After the fixed number of rounds, the player with the most combined points from golem development, completed cards, and quarter control wins.
